anat-gyn-organs.intro: The uterus, cervix, and vagina sit in the middle of the pelvis between the bladder in front and the rectum behind. Learn the organs, their parts, and their neighbors from four views. Explore each view, then switch to Quiz mode.

plates.title: Female Pelvis (Sagittal)
plates.caption: Midline sagittal female pelvis, anterior on the left. The uterus is anteverted, tipped forward over the bladder. Source: Cancer Research UK, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; labels removed. (Diagram CRUK 477)

hotspots.label: Uterine Fundus
hotspots.blurb: Top of the uterus. Fundal endometrial cancers can drain directly to para-aortic nodes via the ovarian vessels.

hotspots.label: Uterine Body (Corpus)
hotspots.blurb: Endometrial cancer starts in its lining. Usually anteverted (tipped forward over the bladder).

hotspots.label: Cervix
hotspots.blurb: Lower, narrow part of the uterus projecting into the vagina. Cervical cancer starts at its transformation zone.

hotspots.label: Vagina
hotspots.blurb: Runs down and forward from the cervix. The upper vagina around the cervix forms the fornices.

hotspots.label: Bladder
hotspots.blurb: In front of the cervix and upper vagina, separated from them by a thin septum. An organ at risk for both pelvic RT and brachytherapy.

hotspots.label: Rectum
hotspots.blurb: Behind the cervix and vagina, across the pouch of Douglas. The organ at risk that most often limits brachytherapy dose.

hotspots.label: Sigmoid Colon
hotspots.blurb: Loops above the uterus; it can drape over the tandem during brachy (sigmoid D2cc).

hotspots.label: Pouch of Douglas (Rectouterine Pouch)
hotspots.blurb: Lowest point of the peritoneal cavity, between the uterus and rectum. Where ascites and peritoneal implants collect.

hotspots.label: Vesicouterine Pouch
hotspots.blurb: Peritoneal recess between the bladder and uterus.

hotspots.label: Pubic Symphysis
hotspots.blurb: Anterior landmark.

hotspots.label: Sacrum
hotspots.blurb: Posterior landmark; the uterosacral ligaments run toward it (presacral node spread).

plates.title: Uterus, Cervix & Adnexa (Coronal)
plates.caption: Coronal uterus, cervix, tubes, and ovaries. Source: Cancer Research UK, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; labels removed. and tumor removed (Diagram CRUK 196)

hotspots.label: Endometrium
hotspots.blurb: Inner lining: where endometrial cancer starts. Tumors grow outward from here into the muscle wall.

hotspots.label: Myometrium
hotspots.blurb: Muscle wall. Sarcomas arise here. The junctional zone is its inner dark band on MRI.

hotspots.label: Serosa
hotspots.blurb: Thin peritoneal covering on the outside of the uterus. Beyond it lie the adnexa, bowel, and peritoneal cavity.

hotspots.label: Internal Os
hotspots.blurb: Top of the cervical canal, where the cervix meets the uterine body (the lower uterine segment).

hotspots.label: External Os / Transformation Zone
hotspots.blurb: Where the squamocolumnar junction sits: the origin of most cervical cancers. The tandem enters here.

hotspots.label: Fallopian Tube
hotspots.blurb: Many high-grade serous 'ovarian' cancers actually start in the fimbriated end of the tube.

hotspots.label: Ovary
hotspots.blurb: Attached to the side wall by the infundibulopelvic ligament, which carries the ovarian vessels and lymphatics up to the para-aortic nodes.

plates.title: The Vagina: Thirds & Walls
plates.caption: Close-up of the sagittal pelvis, anterior on the left: the vagina runs down and forward from the cervix to the introitus, with the bladder and urethra in front and the rectum behind. Source: Cancer Research UK, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; labels removed. (Diagram CRUK 477)

hotspots.label: Vaginal Fornices
hotspots.blurb: Recesses around the cervix. The ovoids or ring of the brachy applicator sit here.

hotspots.label: Upper Third
hotspots.blurb: Surrounds the cervix (the fornices). Drains to the pelvic nodes. After hysterectomy this becomes the vaginal cuff, the target of vaginal brachytherapy.

hotspots.label: Middle Third
hotspots.blurb: Drains to pelvic nodes.

hotspots.label: Lower Third
hotspots.blurb: Ends at the introitus, next to the urethra and anus. Drains to the groin (inguinofemoral) nodes, like the vulva.

hotspots.label: Introitus
hotspots.blurb: Opening of the vagina.

hotspots.label: Anterior Wall (Bladder / Urethra)
hotspots.blurb: Faces the bladder and urethra.

hotspots.label: Posterior Wall (Rectum)
hotspots.blurb: Faces the rectum. Also drains to presacral/perirectal nodes. Rectovaginal septum dose matters in brachy.

plates.title: Vulva & Perineum
plates.caption: External vulva. Source: Cancer Research UK, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; labels removed. (Diagram CRUK 285)

hotspots.label: Mons Pubis
hotspots.blurb: Fatty tissue over the pubic bone.

hotspots.label: Clitoris
hotspots.blurb: Midline. Lymph from midline structures crosses to both groins.

hotspots.label: Labia Majora
hotspots.blurb: Outer hair-bearing folds and the most common site of vulvar cancer. A lesion here, away from the midline, drains mainly to the groin on the same side.

hotspots.label: Labia Minora
hotspots.blurb: Inner folds.

hotspots.label: Urethral Meatus
hotspots.blurb: Sits just above the introitus, close to most vulvar tumors.

hotspots.label: Vaginal Introitus
hotspots.blurb: The vaginal opening, just behind the urethra.

hotspots.label: Bartholin Gland Area
hotspots.blurb: Posterolateral. A solid mass here in an older woman needs a biopsy.

hotspots.label: Perineal Body / Fourchette
hotspots.blurb: Between vagina and anus. Midline.

hotspots.label: Anus
hotspots.blurb: Just behind the perineal body, a few centimeters from the posterior vulva.

anat-gyn-nodes.intro: Each GYN organ drains in its own direction. The cervix and uterus drain to the pelvic and then para-aortic nodes; the vulva and lower vagina drain to the groins. Start with the overall map, then the groin.

plates.title: Pelvic & Para-aortic Nodal Map
plates.caption: Simplified frontal map of the pelvic, para-aortic, and groin nodes around the uterus. Chains are drawn schematically: the obturator nodes sit deep, between the external and internal iliac chains. Source: Cancer Research UK, via Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0; labels removed. (Diagram CRUK 040)

hotspots.label: Para-aortic Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Along the aorta and IVC up to the renal vessels. Reached from the pelvic chain or directly from the uterine fundus and ovaries via the ovarian vessels.

hotspots.label: Common Iliac Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Above the iliac bifurcation. Regional for cervix and endometrium. Positive common iliac nodes usually prompt para-aortic coverage.

hotspots.label: External Iliac Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Along the external iliac vessels at the pelvic brim. One of the main pelvic node groups.

hotspots.label: Internal Iliac (Hypogastric) Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Deep pelvis. First echelon for the cervix.

hotspots.label: Obturator Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Pelvic side wall. First echelon; the most commonly involved node in cervical cancer.

hotspots.label: Presacral Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Reached via the uterosacral ligaments. Included down to about S3 in pelvic fields.

hotspots.label: Parametrial Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Right beside the cervix and uterus.

hotspots.label: Inguinofemoral Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Regional for the vulva and lower vagina; distant for cervix and uterus.

hotspots.label: Uterus / Cervix
hotspots.blurb: The primary.

plates.title: Inguinofemoral (Groin) Nodes
plates.caption: Right femoral triangle from the front (lateral on the left), superficial layer: inguinal ligament, femoral vessels, great saphenous vein, and inguinal nodes (green). Source: Fischerova et al., Ultrasound Obstet Gynecol 2025 (PMC12133214), fig. 19b, CC BY 4.0.

hotspots.label: Inguinal Ligament
hotspots.blurb: Roof of the femoral canal. Superficial nodes run along below it.

hotspots.label: Superficial Inguinal Nodes (Horizontal Group)
hotspots.blurb: Just below and parallel to the inguinal ligament. First echelon for the vulva.

hotspots.label: Superficial Inguinal Nodes (Vertical Group)
hotspots.blurb: Along the great saphenous vein.

hotspots.label: Saphenofemoral Junction
hotspots.blurb: Where the great saphenous vein joins the femoral vein; the center of the superficial nodes.

hotspots.label: Femoral Vein
hotspots.blurb: Nodes lie medial to it. Groin RT fields and dissections center on the femoral vessels.

hotspots.label: Femoral Artery
hotspots.blurb: Lateral to the vein (NAVEL: nerve, artery, vein, empty space, lymphatics).

anat-gyn-drainage.intro: Same map, four different primaries. Click through each site and follow the numbers in order: they trace the path lymph takes from the tumor outward. This is the logic behind every GYN nodal field.

plates.title: Cervix
plates.caption: Cervix: lateral first (parametria and side wall), then up the iliac chain to the para-aortics. Same Cancer Research UK nodal map (Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0).

hotspots.label: Primary: Cervix
hotspots.blurb: Tumor starts at the transformation zone and spreads sideways into the parametria.

hotspots.label: Parametrial Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Small nodes right beside the cervix. The first stop.

hotspots.label: Obturator Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Pelvic side wall. The most commonly involved node group in cervical cancer.

hotspots.label: Internal Iliac Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Deep pelvis along the internal iliac vessels. First echelon with the obturator nodes.

hotspots.label: External Iliac Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Along the external iliac vessels at the pelvic brim.

hotspots.label: Presacral Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Reached along the uterosacral ligaments, which run back from the cervix to the sacrum.

hotspots.label: Common Iliac Nodes
hotspots.blurb: The next step up, above the iliac bifurcation.

hotspots.label: Para-aortic Nodes
hotspots.blurb: The top of the chain. If these are involved, the RT field extends up to the renal vessels.

plates.title: Endometrium
plates.caption: Endometrium: pelvic nodes like the cervix, plus a direct route from the fundus to the para-aortics. Same Cancer Research UK nodal map (Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0).

hotspots.label: Primary: Uterine Body
hotspots.blurb: Endometrial cancer starts in the lining of the uterine body.

hotspots.label: Obturator & Internal Iliac Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Lower uterine tumors drain like the cervix, out to the side wall.

hotspots.label: External Iliac Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Also part of the pelvic chain.

hotspots.label: Common Iliac Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Above the bifurcation, on the way to the para-aortics.

hotspots.label: Ovarian Vessel Route
hotspots.blurb: Lymphatics from the fundus travel with the ovarian vessels in the infundibulopelvic ligament.

hotspots.label: Para-aortic Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Reached directly through the ovarian vessel route, so para-aortic nodes can be positive even when pelvic nodes are negative.

hotspots.label: Inguinal Nodes (Rare)
hotspots.blurb: A rare path along the round ligament, which runs from the uterine horn through the inguinal canal.

plates.title: Vagina
plates.caption: Vagina: the drainage depends on which part of the tube the tumor is in. Same Cancer Research UK nodal map (Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0).

hotspots.label: Primary: Vagina
hotspots.blurb: The vagina is a tube, and each part drains to a different place.

hotspots.label: Upper Vagina to Pelvic Nodes
hotspots.blurb: The upper two-thirds drain like the cervix: obturator and internal and external iliac nodes.

hotspots.label: External Iliac Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Part of the pelvic chain for upper vaginal tumors.

hotspots.label: Posterior Wall to Presacral Nodes
hotspots.blurb: The posterior wall, next to the rectum, also drains to the presacral and perirectal nodes.

hotspots.label: Lower Vagina to Inguinofemoral Nodes
hotspots.blurb: The lower third drains like the vulva, to the groins.

hotspots.label: Common Iliac & Para-aortic Nodes
hotspots.blurb: The next steps up from the pelvic chain.

plates.title: Vulva
plates.caption: Vulva: groins first, then the pelvis. The vulva itself sits just below this drawing. Same Cancer Research UK nodal map (Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0).

hotspots.label: Primary: Vulva (Below the Drawing)
hotspots.blurb: The vulva sits below the vaginal opening. It is skin, and it drains like skin: to the groins.

hotspots.label: Superficial Inguinal Nodes
hotspots.blurb: First echelon. The nodes along the inguinal ligament and the great saphenous vein.

hotspots.label: Deep Femoral Nodes (Cloquet's)
hotspots.blurb: Next, along the femoral vein. Cloquet's node, under the inguinal ligament, is the gateway to the pelvis.

hotspots.label: Opposite Groin
hotspots.blurb: Midline tumors (clitoris, perineal body) drain to both groins, so both are evaluated.

hotspots.label: External Iliac Nodes
hotspots.blurb: Only reached after the groins. For the vulva these count as distant, not regional.
